title: False friends
goal: By the end of this lesson you can avoid the most common French–English false friends and recognise the Quebec anglicisms (canceller, checker, chum) you will hear every day, along with their standard equivalents.

body: A false friend (*un faux ami*) is a French word that looks like an English word but means something different. English and French share thousands of real cognates (*la nation*, *important*, *le restaurant*), which is why the false ones are so dangerous.
Learn them in pairs: the French word and what it really means, plus the French word for the English meaning.
These are the ones English speakers get wrong most often. Study the right-hand column: that is how to say the English meaning in French.
learn.tip: Actuellement = right now. If you mean 'actually', say en fait.

body: Living next to English, Quebec French has borrowed many English words and structures. In casual speech you will hear *canceller* (to cancel), *checker* (to check), *booker* (to book), *parker* (to park) and *un chum* (a boyfriend, or a male friend).

Understand them and use them with friends if you like, but in writing, at work and with strangers, use the standard forms: *annuler*, *vérifier*, *réserver*, *se stationner*. The Office québécois de la langue française (OQLF) actively promotes these standard words.
Note: *se stationner* and *le stationnement* are the normal Quebec words for parking. In France, *se garer* and *le parking* are more common.

body: *Mon chum* usually means 'my boyfriend' or 'my partner' (male). *Un chum* or *mes chums* can also mean buddies. Context tells you which.
The female equivalent is *ma blonde* (my girlfriend, my partner), whatever her hair colour! *Une chum* (or *une amie*) is a female friend. These are very common, friendly, informal Quebec words.

quebec.intro: Quebec speech is full of English verbs with French endings (canceller, checker) and words like chum and blonde. Understand them, use them casually if you want, and keep the standard forms for writing and formal situations.

items.note: Informal; chum can also mean buddy

items.en: My girlfriend is coming with us.

items.note: Calque from English; avoid in writing

items.std: Je me suis stationné en face.
items.note: Informal; se stationner is the Quebec standard

drills.q: Where do you borrow books for free?
drills.why: La bibliothèque = library; la librairie = bookstore.

drills.q: What is the standard French for the Quebec anglicism 'checker'?

drills.why: Ma blonde = my girlfriend/partner, any hair colour.

drills.q: Je t'___ depuis vingt minutes! (to wait)
drills.en: I've been waiting for you for twenty minutes!

drills.q: On doit ___ le souper, ma mère est malade. (to cancel, standard)
drills.en: We have to cancel supper, my mother is sick.

drills.a: Où est-ce qu'on peut se stationner?

a: Je reste à la maison ce soir.
Ce soir, je reste à la maison.
Je reste chez moi ce soir.
Ce soir, je reste chez moi.
Est-ce que vous avez de la monnaie?
Est-ce que tu as de la monnaie?

vocab.ex: En fait, c'est une bonne idée.
On pourra éventuellement changer la date.
Je sors avec mes chums vendredi.
On peut se stationner dans la rue.

pron.tip: Said like English 'chum', but with a French 'o' sound: TCHOM.
ahn FET: the t is pronounced in en fait.

dialogue.fr: Salut! On se voit toujours ce soir?
dialogue.en: Hi! Are we still seeing each other tonight?

dialogue.fr: En fait, je dois annuler. Mon chum est malade.
dialogue.en: Actually, I have to cancel. My boyfriend is sick.
Oh no! What's wrong with him?

dialogue.fr: La grippe. Actuellement, il est au lit.
dialogue.en: The flu. Right now he's in bed.

dialogue.fr: Pas de problème. Je vais checker si le resto peut changer la réservation.
dialogue.en: No problem. I'll check if the restaurant can change the reservation.

dialogue.fr: Merci. On pourrait y aller samedi?
Bonne idée. Je te texte après.
dialogue.en: Good idea. I'll text you after.

questions.q: What does 'actuellement, il est au lit' mean?
What new day do they suggest?

speak.prompt: Say where you are working or studying currently, using 'actuellement'.
speak.model: Actuellement, je travaille dans une entreprise à Montréal.

speak.prompt: Say 'I'll check' and 'I have to cancel' first casually (Quebec), then in standard French.
speak.model: J'vas checker. Je dois canceller. / Je vais vérifier. Je dois annuler.

speak.prompt: Introduce your partner or a friend using chum or blonde.
speak.model: Je te présente mon chum, Alex. / Voici ma blonde, Sophie.

write.prompt: Write a short formal email (4–5 sentences) to cancel an appointment. Use only standard French (no anglicisms).
write.model: Bonjour Madame Tremblay, je vous écris pour annuler mon rendez-vous de jeudi à 14 h. Actuellement, je suis à l'extérieur de la ville. Pourriez-vous vérifier s'il y a une place la semaine prochaine? Merci beaucoup et bonne journée. Alex Martin

quiz.why: It means 'possibly, if necessary', not 'in the end'.

quiz.q: How do you say 'I attended the meeting'?
quiz.why: Assister à = to attend. Attendre = to wait.

quiz.q: Which is the standard Quebec verb for 'to park'?
quiz.why: Se stationner (France often says se garer).

options: a calque from English; standard is 'ça a du sens'
quiz.why: Heard in Quebec, but the standard is avoir du sens.
Rester = to stay; to rest = se reposer.
In the plural, chums usually means friends.

quiz.q: How do you say 'Actually, I'm tired'?
